us12_tech.topic: Tech and venture capital in Israel and the US; R&D intensity; US tech firms in Israel

claims.text: IIA: high-tech about 17% of Israel's GDP (~$317bn GDP context) in 2024; about 57% of exports in H1 2025; exports $78bn in 2024; about 403,000 employees (11.5% of workforce) in H1 2025; employment growth below 2% a year since 2023 vs mostly above 5% the prior decade; R&D employees down 6.5% y/y H1 2025; output 'virtually unchanged in 2024 for a second consecutive year'; fundraising 'returned to 2019-2020 levels'; fifth-largest startup-fundraising hub in 2024

IVC/LeumiTech: Israeli tech private funding $11.1bn in 418 rounds in 2025, up 15% on 2024, deal count down 9%; 180 M&A/IPOs worth $17.7bn; 13 pending deals expected to add $63bn incl. Google's $32bn Wiz
Times of Israel/IVC: Israeli tech companies raised $25.6bn in 2021, of which $18.64bn from foreign investors; Q2 2023 about $1.78bn, down 65% from ~$5bn in Q2 2022
Latest R&D intensity: Israel 6.35% (World Bank 2023), 6.76% (OECD 2024); US 3.45% (World Bank 2023; OECD 2024)

PitchBook-NVCA: US VC deal value $156.1bn (2019), $175.6bn (2020), $358.2bn (2021), $236.2bn (2022), $168.8bn (2023), $213.2bn (2024), $339.4bn (2025); AI/ML 65.4% of 2025 deal value; half of 2025 deal value went to 0.05% of deals; Anthropic $15bn round largest of Q4 2025
Intel in Israel since 1974; 9,335 employees (undated page); exports about $86bn 1974–2023, consistently 3.5–5.5% of Israel's total exports; about $27bn invested 1974–2021

Netanyahu announced 18 June 2023 Intel's $25bn Kiryat Gat investment ('the largest investment by an international company ever in Israel'), with a government grant of 12.8% and a 7.5% tax rate (up from 5%); Globes (26 Dec 2023): grant $3.2bn, the largest the government has given a private company; Intel ~12,000 employees, largest private-sector employer
Calcalist (14 July 2025): Intel Israel ~9,350 employees mid-2025, down from 10,800 in 2023 and peak 12,000 in 2021; ~1,500 left in 2024; doubts over Fab38's future
Nvidia bought Mellanox in 2020 for a reported $6.9bn; planned Kiryat Tivon campus for up to 10,000 employees, biggest outside the US, initial occupancy 2031
Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): '3 out of every 5 shekels raised in 2025 were invested in cyber or organizational software companies'

us12_defence.topic: Defence industry and arms exports, Israel and US

claims.text: IMOD: 2025 defence export deals $19.2bn, up nearly 30% on 2024, fifth straight record; more than doubled in five years and quadrupled in a decade; G2G about $10bn; Europe 36%, Asia-Pacific 32%, MENA 15%, North America 13%, Latin America 2%, Africa 2%; air defence 29%, observation/optronics 22%; Baram: force buildup budget 'relies heavily on these partnerships'

Globes: Abraham Accords countries 15% of 2025 deals (12% in 2024); Europe 54% in 2024 inflated by Arrow 3 sale to Germany (~$3.5bn); air defence 48% in 2024, 36% in 2023; SIBAT's Kulas: Israel no longer the only country with a 'combat-proven' label
Israel defence exports $12.5bn in 2022 and record $13.1bn in 2023 (MoD report 17 June 2024); doubled over five years; missile/rocket/air defence 36% in 2023

SIPRI 2021–25: US 42% of global arms exports (36% in 2016–20), volume +27%; top US recipients Saudi Arabia 12%, Ukraine 9.4%, Japan 8.9%; Israel 7th supplier, 4.4% (3.1% in 2016–20), exports +56%; recipients India 29%, Germany 21%, US 7.8%; Israel 14th importer (1.9%), imports +12%, US 68% and Germany 31% of supply
State Department figures (via Defense Archives): FY2025 US arms transfers $331.18bn (DCS $226.8bn, FMS $104.4bn); FY2024 $318.7bn; FMS down 11.47% in FY2025
State Department FY2023 summary: FMS $51.9bn (FY2022), $80.9bn (FY2023); DCS $153.6bn (FY2022), $157.5bn (FY2023)

us12_other.topic: Energy, food and agriculture, pharma, finance in Israel and the US

claims.text: Israel gas production 27.38 bcm in 2024 (25.28 bcm 2023): Leviathan 11.33, Tamar 10.09, Karish 5.96; exports to Egypt and Jordan 13.11 bcm (11.56 in 2023); domestic 14.27 bcm (52%)

Gas framework (Aug 2015): Delek to sell Tamar, Karish and Tanin holdings within six years; US-based Noble Energy to cut Tamar stake to max 25%; regulated prices for six years; government bound 10 years; antitrust commissioner David Gilo resigned in May 2015 over Noble and Delek's dominance; Tamar producing since 2013; Leviathan to be developed by 2019

Leviathan consortium signed $35bn deal to sell about 130 bcm to Egypt through 2040 (Aug 2025); triples previous export volumes; ~13% of Israel's reserves; NewMed (formerly Delek Drilling, Tshuva's Delek Group) 45.3%
EIA (via Reuters): US dry gas production 103.2 Bcf/d in 2024, forecast 107.1 (2025) and 107.4 (2026)

State Comptroller (Jan 2024): Israel's price level 27% above OECD average (PPP); food prices 37% above OECD and 51% above EU; ten largest food suppliers held more than 50% of the food and consumer products market; abnormal profit among food and pharmaceutical importers; 46 food products under price supervision; imported butter up ~60% after removal from tight supervision in Nov 2021
USDA ERS: four largest beef packers' share of steer and heifer purchases 36% (1980), 81% (1995), 85% (latest); farm-to-wholesale spread no persistent rise 1980–2015, widened sharply after 2015

Teva (14 Dec 2017): ~14,000 job cuts (over 25% of workforce) over two years, ~1,700 in Israel, Jerusalem plant to close; ~$10bn debt due within 12 months; bought Actavis Generics for about $40bn; dividend suspended; Histadrut called a general strike; ~6,800 employees in Israel

Competition Authority (26 Mar 2024) planned to declare Leumi, Hapoalim, Discount, Mizrahi Tefahot and First International a concentration group; the five held 98% of banking assets at end-2022, Leumi and Hapoalim 57%

Audit re-fetch (21 Oct 2026): Netanyahu said the deal would bring 'hundreds of billions of shekels' to citizens; Finance Minister Kahlon said he would oppose it without 'more stringent price controls'
